title: Am, Is or Are? The Verb 'To Be'

body.heading: One verb, three costumes
paragraphs: The verb 'to be' changes its costume depending on who we are talking about. When you talk about yourself, it wears am. When you talk about one other person or thing, it wears is. When you talk about more than one, or about you and we, it wears are.
Say each sentence out loud. Your ear will start to know which costume sounds right.

body.heading: I am
paragraphs: I am a reader. I am happy today. I am ready to learn.
Am belongs to I — only I, every time.

body.heading: He is, she is, it is
paragraphs: He is my brother. She is a good friend. It is a sunny day.
One person or one thing? Choose is.

body.heading: You are, we are, they are
paragraphs: You are kind. We are a team. They are birds in the garden.
Talking to someone, talking about a group, or talking about more than one thing? Choose are.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Finish these sentences about your family: 'I am…', 'Mom or Dad is…', 'We are…'.
2. Point at things around the room and say 'It is…' sentences. How many can you make in one minute?

takeaway: I am; he, she and it is; you, we and they are — the verb 'to be' changes with who you are talking about.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity or materials are involved.
screenFreeExtension: After reading, close the screen and retell three things you learned to someone at home in your own words.
